data.reason: This settles D2.f2: I keep v2 (block_k 2) and do not revert to block_k 3. The revert worsens every customer measure. On-time falls from 272.6 to 264.6 (-8.0, 0/5 seeds improved), late rises from 2.0 to 10.0, p95_wait_s rises from 90.0 to 121, blocked s rises from 1102 to 1855, and the lowest on-time rate falls from 0.98 to 0.93. It fails the improvement gate, and customers, who have no vote, would bear the whole cost. D2 and D3 set a condition: I would reconsider the revert if road violations persisted or grew. Under v2 they are 29.6 this period, down from 34.8 in period 3 and close to the 28.0 accepted in D2. The condition is therefore not triggered now, though violations remain above the pre-v2 level and their safety meaning is unknown. C's utility under v2 is 68.8, its highest so far in these measurements, so the case for compensating C at customers' expense is weaker than in D2. The revert would give C +8.9 and B +4.3 while costing A 5.2. B and C voted for it, but a company majority does not override a measured loss to customers on the KPI's main goal. I follow the LLM's recommendation. Violations should be addressed with a targeted rule rather than a blanket revert of blocking relief. Keeping v2 means road violations stay at 29.6 for now, which is an unknown safety cost I accept and will keep monitoring.
assumptions: Road violations at around 29.6 per period do not represent an immediate serious safety hazard.
This period's measurements are representative of the effect of block_k under busy + rush demand.
B and C will continue to operate normally despite another decision against their preference.
unknowns: The safety meaning of road violations, and the level the town and other road users find acceptable.
Whether violations under v2 will grow again under next period's demand.
Whether a targeted rule exists that reduces violations without lowering on-time deliveries.
How B and C will respond strategically to repeated decisions against their vote.
How customers perceive the difference between 2 and 10 late deliveries and between p95 waits of 90 s and 121 s.
